title: Scalar rigidity of a pinned potential dualizing complex
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $r\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring], let $\delta$ be a dimension function, and let $K$ be a pinned potential dualizing complex for $(X,\delta,\Lambda)$ [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. For derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and ordinary truncation [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], the scalar-action map is an isomorphism $$\Lambda_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau_{\leq0}R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(K,K).$$ Thus $\mathcal H^aR\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(K,K)=0$ for $a<0$, and scalar multiplication identifies $\Lambda_X$ with $\mathcal H^0R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(K,K)$.

source.place: Expose XVII, Theorem 5.1.1, scalar derived-endomorphism assertion

proof.text: Call the scalar assertion $P(T,\delta)$, quantified over every pinned potential complex on $T$. We prove it for all Noetherian excellent schemes with invertible $\ell$. The existence and unique pinning-preserving isomorphism assertions needed in the gluing lemma are already supplied independently by [lem-per-potential-dualizing-uniqueness]; we use only those two clauses of its statement, not the stronger assertion inside its proof. The empty scheme satisfies $P$: its sheaf category is zero and the scalar map is the unique isomorphism $0\to0$.

source.place: XVII, Theorem 5.1.1 and subsection 5.5: the three assertions propagated together

proof.text: Reduction preserves and reflects $P$. Indeed $a:T_{\mathrm{red}}\to T$ is a universal homeomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], and [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] gives the inverse/direct-image equivalence of small etale topoi. Applied to module sheaves and then termwise to complexes, this exact equivalence identifies coefficient sheaves, Hom complexes, injectives, and cohomology, hence derived internal Hom and ordinary truncation. The image of scalar multiplication is scalar multiplication. It also identifies the support kernel for each closed point in each local scheme: the complementary open and restriction map correspond. Thus the residue-field costalks correspond. In [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex] the residue transitions are computed from reduced one-dimensional closures in strict localizations and their normalizations; reduction leaves these curves, degrees, roots of unity, and trait complexes unchanged. The same pinnings therefore make $a^*K$ potential for the same dimension function. Reduction is again Noetherian excellent, since on affines it is a quotient finite-type algebra and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] applies. We may consequently assume a scheme reduced whenever proving $P$.

source.place: XVII, subsection 5.5: reduction to the reduced case; Definitions 1.4.1 and 2.1.1-2.1.2

proof.text: For a normal scheme, [rem-pc-regular-normal], clause (2), gives finitely many disjoint open-and-closed normal integral components. On one component with generic point $\eta$, set $m=\delta(\eta)$ and $K_0=K(-m)[-2m]$. The twist line is invertible: [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] makes positive powers etale locally free of rank one; the negative powers in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex] are their module duals, and evaluation is an isomorphism because it is so after choosing a local basis. Tensoring by this line and shifting changes each pinning to $\Lambda(\delta(x)-m)[2\delta(x)-2m]$. On an etale cover trivializing the line, both the supported complexes and their residue maps are the original ones tensored by its basis; thus the compatibility equation is preserved. The resulting dimension function has generic value zero. Apply the scalar clause of [lem-per-normal-pinned-extension] to $K_0$. Locally, simultaneous tensoring of the two entries of the Hom complex by a free rank-one module cancels, as do their simultaneous shifts; these identifications are independent of the basis and take scalar action to scalar action. The Hom model [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] therefore identifies the scalar assertions for $K_0$ and $K$. Restriction to the finitely many disjoint components detects cohomology and isomorphisms, so $P$ holds on every normal scheme.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 5.3.1(c), with twist/shift normalization of the generic dimension value

proof.text: Fix the original scheme $X$. Use Noetherian induction on closed subsets $S\subseteq|X|$, with the strengthened assertion: $P(T,\epsilon)$ holds for every Noetherian excellent scheme $T$ finite over the reduced closed subscheme $S_{\mathrm{red}}$, and every dimension function $\epsilon$ on $T$. The empty support was settled in Step 1. Assume the assertion for every proper closed subset of $S$, and take such a $T$. By Step 2 replace $T$ by $T_{\mathrm{red}}$. This remains finite over $S_{\mathrm{red}}$: a quotient of a finite module is finite. Its image $C$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. If $C\subsetneq S$, the reduced $T$ factors through $C_{\mathrm{red}}$: on affine charts each element of the radical ideal defining $C$ maps to an element lying in every prime of the reduced source ring, hence to zero. This factor map is finite since the same module generators work after passing to the quotient of the base ring. The induction hypothesis applies. We may therefore assume $T\to S_{\mathrm{red}}$ is surjective.

source.place: XVII, subsection 5.5: Noetherian induction strengthened to schemes finite over a closed support

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation] to this reduced $T$. Its normalization $p:T'\to T$ is finite surjective, its source is Noetherian excellent and normal, and it is an isomorphism above a dense open $U$ containing all generic points of $T$. Let $Y=(T\setminus U)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $Y'=Y\times_TT'$, and $q:Y'\to T$. These are Noetherian excellent schemes: affine rings of $Y$ are quotients, and those of $Y'$ are finite algebras over affine rings of $Y$, so [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] applies. Invertibility of $\ell$ pulls back. Finite maps are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], so the identity open immersion followed by each of $p,i:Y\hookrightarrow T,q$ is a compactification. Apply [lem-per-potential-dualizing-finite-pullback] to a pinned potential complex on $T$, which exists by Step 1. It supplies dimension functions on $T',Y,Y'$, equal to $\epsilon$ composed with the structure maps: a residue extension of a finite morphism is finite, hence has transcendence degree zero. These are precisely the induced dimension functions required by the gluing statement.

source.place: XVII, subsection 5.5: the normalization square; Proposition 2.4.3.1 for induced dimension functions

proof.text: The image of $Y$ in $S$ is a proper closed subset. Closedness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. To check properness, a point of $T$ above a generic point of $S$ is generic in $T$. On affine charts the base prime $\mathfrak p$ is minimal. If its source prime $\mathfrak q$ were not minimal, take a minimal prime $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\mathfrak q$. Its contraction is contained in $\mathfrak p$, hence equals $\mathfrak p$. The finite algebra is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] rules this out. The boundary $Y$ contains no generic point of $T$, hence its image contains no generic point of $S$. Both $Y$ and $Y'$ are finite over $S$: on affines, if $b_j$ generate a finite algebra over the base and $c_k$ generate a second finite algebra over the first, the products $b_jc_k$ generate the composite. Their images lie in the same proper closed subset $C$. Reduce them first using Step 2; the reduced sources factor finitely through $C_{\mathrm{red}}$ by the radical-ideal argument of Step 4. The induction hypothesis then supplies $P$ on $Y_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $Y'_{\mathrm{red}}$, for the transferred dimension functions. Step 2 restores $P$ on $Y$ and $Y'$, including any nilpotents in the fibre product.

source.place: XVII, subsection 5.5: why the two boundary schemes fall under the strengthened induction hypothesis

proof.text: Step 3 supplies scalar rigidity on the normal scheme $T'$, and Step 6 supplies it on $Y,Y'$. Step 1 gives existence and unique pinned isomorphisms on all three schemes. The finite square of Step 5 satisfies every hypothesis of [lem-per-finite-modification-pinned-gluing], with the induced dimension functions just checked. Its statement therefore gives scalar rigidity for every potential complex on $T$. This proves the inductive assertion for $S$; Step 2 also covers its originally nonreduced sources. Noetherian induction closes, and taking $S=|X|$ and the identity map from $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ to itself proves $P(X_{\mathrm{red}},\delta)$, hence $P(X,\delta)$ by Step 2. The map supplied by the gluing statement is explicitly scalar action, so no arbitrary choice of a pinned isomorphism replaces the requested map.

source.place: XVII, subsection 5.5, concluding application of Proposition 5.4.1

proof.text: Set $H=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(K,K)$. The scalar map $\Lambda_X\to H$ factors uniquely through $\tau_{\leq0}H$ by the truncation adjunction in [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], since $\Lambda_X$ lies in degree zero. Steps 1-7 show that this factor is an isomorphism. By [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], truncation preserves cohomology in degrees at most zero, whereas $\Lambda_X$ has cohomology only in degree zero. It follows that $\mathcal H^aH=0$ for $a<0$ and that the scalar map identifies $\mathcal H^0H$ with $\Lambda_X$, as asserted.
